scope: Adversarial review of the planned end-to-end user and agent experience and human-needed policy, from a vague idea through clarification, ready ticket, build, review, maintenance, waiting, escalation, notification, and exception handling. Reviewed the required research corpus, docs/**, .agent-os/**, src/**, migrations/**, tests/**, and tests-sql/** only where they make the plan concrete or contradict it. Expected absence of a production controller was not treated as a defect. Repeated copies of claims were treated as one evidence lineage.
strengths: The design clearly states that agents only propose and that consequential actions require deterministic policy plus exact-content human approval.
The end-to-end documentation gives concise clarification guidance: one owned question, bounded options, trade-offs, a recommendation, evidence, and a deadline.
The research recognizes human-load controls such as batching questions, pausing after a reminder, deduplicating signals, and never treating silence as consent.
The checked-in JSON schemas and plan-only CLI show an intent to make tickets, decisions, approvals, and reconciliation reviewable rather than leaving them in chat.

findings.title: The plan has incompatible configuration, factory, and decision contracts
findings.requirement: The plan must nominate one versioned, machine-checkable contract for each artifact so the proposed compiler and user workflow are unambiguous.
findings.reproduction: From the repository root run `.venv/bin/agent-os config-validate`, `.venv/bin/agent-os factory-validate .agent-os/factories/ideation.yaml`, and `.venv/bin/agent-os decision-validate .agent-os/factories/example.conversation-decision.json`. All fail with Pydantic validation errors because the Python models describe different shapes. `agent-os demo --factory .agent-os/factories/ideation.yaml` also fails.
findings.impact: The plan does not identify an authoritative executable contract. An implementer or fresh adopter cannot tell which shape the proposed compiler must consume.
findings.recommendation: Choose one versioned contract per artifact, generate or align Python models and JSON Schemas from it, document the CLI invocation, and make all checked-in examples pass both validators.
findings.verification: Add an end-to-end smoke test that installs the package, validates `.agent-os/config.yaml`, every registered factory, and every example, then runs `agent-os demo --factory` for each executable example.

findings.title: Generic factory guards require future-stage gates and deadlock the happy path
findings.requirement: Each transition must evaluate only gates that are available at that phase; early ideation and planning cannot require later approval, lease, verification, or review artifacts.
findings.reproduction: Inspect each factory: every normal edge uses `phase artifacts complete and configured gates pass`, while the global gate list includes final ticket acceptance in ideation and current lease, exact-SHA checks, and risk review in build. Evaluate `PLAN -> READY_REVIEW` or `DISCOVER -> DIVERGE` literally: required downstream artifacts do not yet exist, so the guard cannot pass.
findings.impact: A conforming controller either deadlocks on the first transition or must invent undocumented phase-specific semantics, making review and human expectations non-portable.
findings.recommendation: Represent gates as typed, phase-bound IDs. List exactly which artifacts and decisions each edge requires. Reject forward references unless explicitly modeled as deferred gates.
findings.verification: Compile every factory and execute a happy-path trace with artifact availability checked at each edge; prove no edge requires an artifact first produced in a later phase.

findings.title: The installation plan requires human role bindings that the consumer contract cannot represent
findings.requirement: A consumer must be able to bind each required human role to authenticated principals before any human-needed gate can compile or run.
findings.reproduction: Follow the installation contract in `docs/operations.md`, which says the manifest pins risk/owner role bindings. Try to add product owner, technical owner, security owner, on-call, deploy reviewer, exception owner, or promoter bindings to `consumer.example.yaml`. `consumer.schema.json` has no such fields and rejects additions because `additionalProperties` is false. The central config also contains no principal-to-role mapping.
findings.impact: The compiler cannot verify the planned human intervention matrix. A fresh adopter has no authoritative place to say who receives a question or who may approve each tier.
findings.recommendation: Add a versioned role-binding schema with provider/organization/repository scope, principal identifiers, teams, eligible roles, separation constraints, fallback/on-call mapping, validity period, and provenance. Include it in the effective-config digest.
findings.verification: Validate an example consumer with all roles used by the human intervention matrix; reject missing roles, self-conflicting roles, ambiguous teams, removed principals, and insufficient risk-tier quorum.

findings.title: The maintenance factory omits the documented maintenance lifecycle and outcomes
findings.requirement: Maintenance must preserve signal correlation, suppression with expiry, scheduling, observation, rollback, resurface, and explicit resolution/follow-up ownership.
findings.reproduction: Compare the factory phases (`SCAN, TRIAGE, PLAN, READY_REVIEW, EXECUTE, VERIFY, REVIEW, COMPLETE`) with the documented states (`SIGNAL_RECEIVED, CORRELATED, DIAGNOSED, PROPOSED, SCHEDULED, EXECUTING, VERIFIED, OBSERVING, RESOLVED` plus `SUPPRESSED`, `BLOCKED`, `CANCELLED`, `ROLLED_BACK`). There are no suppress, expiry/resurface, observe, rollback, or explicit resolved edges/artifacts.
findings.impact: A fresh operator cannot represent routine noise suppression or verify that remediation held. `COMPLETE` can conceal an unobserved or rolled-back outcome.
findings.recommendation: Align the factory with the documented durable maintenance state machine and define required signal-group, suppression, schedule, observation, remediation receipt, rollback, and follow-up artifacts.
findings.verification: Run transition coverage tests for success, duplicate signal, suppression expiry, remediation delegated to BUILD, observation failure, rollback, cancellation, and resurface.

findings.title: Ideation retry targets an undefined clarification state
findings.requirement: A vague idea must support an explicit, durable question/wait/answer/resume loop rather than strand the user after budget or retry exhaustion.
findings.reproduction: In `ideation.yaml`, `retry.on_exhaustion` is `NEEDS_CLARIFICATION`, but that value is absent from `phases` and no transition enters or exits it. Exhaust retries in any phase and attempt to resume after an answer; the factory has no legal resume edge.
findings.impact: The exact uncertain-input path advertised by ideation becomes a dead end or requires controller-specific behavior outside the factory.
findings.recommendation: Add a real `NEEDS_INPUT`/`NEEDS_CLARIFICATION` phase with question artifact, owner, deadline, reminder policy, resume token, answer validation, return phase, cancellation, and expiry behavior.
findings.verification: Execute a trace from DISCOVER to clarification, append a valid answer, resume the saved phase, and also test expiry, withdrawal, and cancellation.

findings.title: Normal change-request loops are absent from the build and ticket-review factories
findings.requirement: Human reviewers must be able to request a revision, receive a new digest, and re-review without converting ordinary feedback into an exception/block.
findings.reproduction: The reviewer prompt allows `request_changes` and the canonical lifecycle permits `REVIEW -> IMPLEMENTING`. The build factory permits REVIEW only to HANDOFF or BLOCKED. Ideation permits TICKET_REVIEW only to COMPLETE or BLOCKED. Follow a normal reviewer request for a small correction: neither factory has a review-to-edit/synthesis edge.
findings.impact: Routine back-and-forth is misclassified as BLOCKED or handled outside durable state, losing revision, invalidation, and reviewer context.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit `REVIEW -> IMPLEMENT` and `TICKET_REVIEW -> SYNTHESIZE/CLARIFY` loops. Require a new artifact revision, digest recomputation, stale approval invalidation, and capped repair rounds.
findings.verification: Test one and multiple change-request rounds, a changed head, exhausted repair budget, and final acceptance on the newest digest only.

findings.title: BLOCKED has no durable owner, deadline, saved prior state, or complete resume route
findings.requirement: Every named wait must expose why it waits, who must act, by when, how it resumes, and what happens on silence.
findings.reproduction: Move an item from VERIFYING, REVIEW, or MERGE_QUEUED to BLOCKED. The YAML BLOCKED transitions do not permit return to those states despite the architecture promising return to an explicitly saved prior state. The work_items table stores only lifecycle_state/risk/title/spec reference; Project fields include a blocked reason but no owner, deadline, prior state, or resume token.
findings.impact: Human work can sit silently and cannot be resumed according to the declared state machine. Any reminder implementation would lack authoritative recipient and due time.
findings.recommendation: Add a typed wait record with prior state, reason code, blocking fields, responsible principal, created/due timestamps, notification/dedupe state, escalation path, and resume token. Derive resume edges from the saved state and recheck relevant gates.
findings.verification: For every nonterminal state, test block, display owner/deadline, one deduplicated reminder, answer/unblock to the saved state, expiry escalation, cancellation, and restart recovery.

findings.title: A conversation decision can be marked answered with no answer
findings.requirement: An answered clarification must contain an attributable, timely answer selecting or explicitly overriding the offered choices.
findings.reproduction: Load the example JSON, change only `status` to `answered`, leave `answer` as null, and validate it against `conversation-decision.schema.json` with Draft 2020-12 validation. It has zero schema errors. If an answer object is supplied, `option_id` also is not checked against the declared option IDs.
findings.impact: An agent/controller can resume planning while the decision remains unresolved or cites a nonexistent choice, so apparent human input is not verifiable.
findings.recommendation: Add conditional schema requirements: open requires null/no answer; answered requires a non-null answer and answer event. Enforce option membership and authenticate/authorize the decision actor in controller code.
findings.verification: Add negative tests for answered/null, unknown option, missing answer event, unauthorized actor, expired response, and answer after withdrawal.

findings.title: Exception approvals cannot encode the exception evidence required by the operating model
findings.requirement: Exceptions must bind exact SHA/scope, reason, compensating controls, expiry, owner, and incident/follow-up reference.
findings.reproduction: Set `purpose` to `exception` in an approval that validates today. Attempt to add `scope`, `reason`, `compensating_controls`, or `follow_up`; `additionalProperties: false` rejects them, and none is conditionally required. `candidate_sha` remains optional/null.
findings.impact: Humans cannot create a machine-verifiable exception that meets the documented rule. Controllers must rely on free text elsewhere or accept an under-specified waiver.
findings.recommendation: Define a dedicated exception schema or conditional payload with exact subject/SHA, bounded scope, rationale, compensating controls, owner, issue/incident, expiry, non-waivable controls, and revocation.
findings.verification: Test missing fields, overbroad scope, expired exception, wrong SHA, prohibited waiver, agent self-grant, and successful use only for the exact declared action.

findings.title: The plan names deadlines but does not define a bounded notification and silence policy
findings.requirement: Every human-needed wait must define delivery channel, acknowledgement, reminder cadence/cap, deduplication, escalation, and safe timeout behavior so silence neither authorizes work nor creates spam.
findings.reproduction: Trace `NEEDS_INPUT`, `NEEDS_CLARIFICATION`, readiness approval, review, unknown effect, deploy approval, and exception expiry through the plan. The docs sometimes require an owner/deadline, while the research recommends a reminder then pause, but the plan/config defines no notification channel, acknowledgement, reminder count/cadence, dedupe key, escalation destination, quiet hours, batching, or timeout transition.
findings.impact: Different controller implementers can either wait silently or repeatedly page humans. Users cannot predict where a request arrives or what happens if they do not respond.
findings.recommendation: Add one typed human-interaction policy shared by all factories: severity, channel, recipient resolution, digest-linked action, acknowledgement, batching, reminder cap/cadence, dedupe key, due time, escalation, quiet-hours exception, expiry, and fail-closed terminal/pause behavior.
findings.verification: Simulate each human-needed event with answer, duplicate event, no response, unavailable owner, and controller restart. Verify bounded notification count, stable dedupe, visible ownership/deadline, no consent from silence, and deterministic pause/cancel/escalate.

residual_uncertainty: The repository explicitly describes the deliverable as a proposed plan. This review therefore reports contradictions and missing decision-grade contracts, not the expected absence of production controller/provider implementations.
No usability study, pilot transcript, or measured notification volume exists. The likely human burden cannot be quantified until the plan defines an interaction policy and is exercised in shadow.

Some factory guard phrases may have intended semantics not expressed in the YAML. Confidence is high that the checked-in plan is ambiguous; the eventual compiler could choose a safe interpretation only after that interpretation is specified.
Research results frequently reuse the same vendor or first-party sources. Those repetitions were not counted as independent validation.
